raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #60004. With `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=LHBNC`, `OffloadingConnector` offloads only head 0 of layer 0 per block, so CPU-tier hits return wrong output; reject that layout at registration instead.

### User case

1. A user sets `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=LHBNC` and enables native CPU offload.
2. In `register_kv_caches`, a layer's block stride (`N*C`, 8 KiB) differs from its page (`H*N*C`, 64 KiB), so the layer takes the packed-layout branch meant for DSv4, where the stride exceeds the page.
3. That branch offloads `block_stride` bytes per block, which is head 0 of layer 0, and the block is still counted as stored and later as a hit.
4. A request whose prefix comes back from the CPU tier decodes from mostly unrestored KV. On DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B a 64K-token prompt stores 33.5 MB instead of 12.9 GB, and a question about Gutenberg is answered with ` _1401401010…` instead of ` Johannes Gutenberg … around 1440.`

The fix raises a `ValueError` in `register_kv_caches` when an attention layer's block stride is smaller than its page, naming the layer, both sizes and a layout to use instead.

Unchanged: LBHNC (the connector's preferred layout), LBNHC and the block-outermost layouts take the same paths as before. A one-head (MLA) cache under LHBNC has stride equal to page and is still accepted.

Not a duplicate: no open issue or PR covers this. The open PRs touching the offloading worker (#53544, #56076, #59265) change mapping placement, pointer resolution and quantized-layout preference, not this check. The stride comparison came in with #51718.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/
```

`test_register_kv_caches_covers_whole_page` builds the KV cache for every `KVCacheLayout`, for full attention and single-head MLA, the way the engine does, marks one block in every layer, and checks that the offloaded regions hold all of its bytes. Attention under LHBNC must raise instead; MLA under LHBNC must still pass. The test fails on main.

## Test Result

```text
main:     1 failed, 490 passed  (test_register_kv_caches_covers_whole_page[attention-KVCacheLayout.LHBNC]: DID NOT RAISE)
this PR:  491 passed
```

| DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B, A100 | LBNHC | LHBNC before | LHBNC after |
|---|---|---|---|
| GPU→CPU bytes, 64K-token prompt | 12.9 GB | 33.5 MB | — |
| output after a CPU-tier hit | correct | wrong | startup error |

<details>
<summary>Measurement details</summary>

- Unit tests: this PR (df152cb83) Python sources on a vLLM 0.30.0 precompiled build (torch 2.13.0+cu129), A100 80GB PCIe, driver 575.51.03; also 675 passed after merging main (08d94f017), where main alone fails the same LHBNC case. `register_kv_caches` is the same in 0.30.0 and main apart from the HiSparse condition.
- Engine runs: vLLM 0.30.0 with and without this patch, `--num-gpu-blocks-override 4500 --max-model-len 71936 --enforce-eager --kv-offloading-size 30 --kv-offloading-backend native`. Each check sends a 7,060-token prompt at temperature 0, then a 71,900-token prompt that evicts it from the GPU cache, then the first prompt again. Byte counts are deltas of `vllm:kv_offload_total_bytes_total`.
- Engine runs used the first revision of this patch; the review changes only move the check (same condition and message).
- With this patch, LBNHC still returns identical output for the first request, an immediate repeat and the CPU-tier hit; LHBNC stops at startup with `block stride 8192 B < page 65536 B`.
- This PR only stops the silent corruption. Supporting LHBNC would mean offloading one `N*C` slice per (block, layer, head) (8 KiB here, H times more descriptors, all below the 28 KiB DMA/Triton cutoff) plus per-head canonical mappings, or letting connectors declare the layouts they can handle during layout resolution. I left that to a design discussion (see the issue) and am happy to help with it.

</details>

AI assistance (Claude) was used for the investigation, code and tests. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and measurements on my own hardware.

🚀
What is the reason to force `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=LHBNC`?

@vadiklyutiy Sorry for the slow reply. Nothing forces LHBNC by default: OffloadingConnector asks for LBHNC, and resolution uses it whenever the backends allow. LHBNC comes in only when the user sets `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=LHBNC`, which overrides the connector's preference. On ROCm that is a natural choice: `rocm_attn` lists LHBNC first because its native HIP kernels need H outermost, and under LBHNC it falls back to the Triton kernels. Before this PR, that setting plus CPU offload ran without a warning and returned wrong output after a CPU-tier hit; now it stops at startup. #59999 is the FlashInfer side of the same layout.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.
Can we centralize the layout checks and add the MLA case below?

Can we centralize these checks in `OffloadingConnectorWorker.register_kv_caches()`? Both CPU and Tiered go through it.

I think the right place is after selecting the groups, before building the byte views or taking the packed path. We still have the original tensors and specs there.

I don't want us adding a different gate for every layout. We should have one place checking whether we can offload the full cache correctly, using the actual strides and specs. Let's reuse the same calculations for validation and transfer setup.

We can start with this check here and track the remaining work in #63718.

+def _layer_kv_caches(
+    kv_cache_groups: tuple[KVCacheGroupSpec, ...],
+    kv_caches: dict[str, torch.Tensor],
+    num_blocks: int,
+) -> dict[str, tuple[KVCacheSpec, torch.Tensor]]:
+    """Each layer's spec and KV cache, with manager blocks as dim 0."""
+    layers: dict[str, tuple[KVCacheSpec, torch.Tensor]] = {}
+    for kv_cache_group in kv_cache_groups:
+        assert not kv_cache_group.host_resident
+        group_kv_cache_spec = kv_cache_group.kv_cache_spec
+        if isinstance(group_kv_cache_spec, UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs):
+            per_layer_specs = group_kv_cache_spec.kv_cache_specs
+        else:
+            per_layer_specs = {}
+        for layer_name in kv_cache_group.layer_names:
+            layers[layer_name] = (
+                per_layer_specs.get(layer_name, group_kv_cache_spec),
+                group_kernel_blocks(kv_caches[layer_name], num_blocks),
+            )
+    return layers
+
+
+def _block_stride_bytes(spec: KVCacheSpec, kv_cache: torch.Tensor) -> int:
+    """Bytes from one manager block of a layer's KV cache to the next.
+
+    Packed layouts (e.g. DSv4) interleave layers per block, so this exceeds
+    page_size_bytes; LHBNC puts a block's heads a whole layer of blocks apart,
+    so it falls short. Other layouts match page_size_bytes."""
+    if not isinstance(spec, AttentionSpec):
+        return spec.page_size_bytes
+    return kv_cache.stride(0) * kv_cache.element_size()
+
+
+def _check_offloadable(layers: dict[str, tuple[KVCacheSpec, torch.Tensor]]) -> None:
+    """Fail closed on KV caches the transfers cannot copy whole: a block copied
+    in part still counts as stored, so a later hit would load wrong KV."""
+    for layer_name, (spec, kv_cache) in layers.items():
+        page = spec.page_size_bytes
+        block_stride_bytes = _block_stride_bytes(spec, kv_cache)
+        if block_stride_bytes < page:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"OffloadingConnector cannot offload layer {layer_name}: "
+                f"its KV cache page is not contiguous within a block "
+                f"(block stride {block_stride_bytes} B < page {page} B), "
+                f"as with the LHBNC KV cache layout. Use a layout whose "
+                f"pages are contiguous, e.g. VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=LBHNC."
+            )

Can we centralize these checks in `OffloadingConnectorWorker.register_kv_caches()`? Both CPU and Tiered go through it.

I think the right place is after selecting the groups, before building the byte views or taking the packed path. We still have the original tensors and specs there.

I don't want us adding a different gate for every layout. We should have one place checking whether we can offload the full cache correctly, using the actual strides and specs. Let's reuse the same calculations for validation and transfer setup.

We can start with this check here and track the remaining work in #63718.

What is the reason to force `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=LHBNC`?

@vadiklyutiy Sorry for the slow reply. Nothing forces LHBNC by default: OffloadingConnector asks for LBHNC, and resolution uses it whenever the backends allow. LHBNC comes in only when the user sets `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=LHBNC`, which overrides the connector's preference. On ROCm that is a natural choice: `rocm_attn` lists LHBNC first because its native HIP kernels need H outermost, and under LBHNC it falls back to the Triton kernels. Before this PR, that setting plus CPU offload ran without a warning and returned wrong output after a CPU-tier hit; now it stops at startup. #59999 is the FlashInfer side of the same layout.
